summary: Iter 18: Comprehensive test of ANIP/1.0 Neural Interface, Live Web Uplink, In-Band Autosynth, plus core regression. 24/24 backend pytest tests PASS. Frontend BCI screen, terminal slash commands (/uplink /web /decode /neural), and chat autosynth 'plot 5 1 8 3 9' all work end-to-end with SYNTH-IMAGE rendered inline.
critical_code_review_comments: NeuralInterfaceScreen.jsx: substrate `busy` state is per-kind but button `disabled={!!busy}` disables ALL substrate buttons during any op — expected. However when Playwright fires clicks in rapid succession right after an axios completes, there was one observed miss where the propagate click appeared not to update UI (result panel still showed prior lattice run). Repro standalone worked. Consider debouncing or explicit loading spinner on the specific button, and confirm the click handler no-ops when busy is truthy (currently the button is disabled at HTML level so React should skip).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all critical flows: BCI acquire+decode, all 3 substrate engines, 4 slash commands, chat autosynth plot with inline SYNTH-IMAGE)

seed_data_creation: chat session 'test-e2e-autosynth' created with 1 turn; several neural sessions logged via /api/neural/synthetic and /api/neural/decode
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_iter18.py. Neural decode/edf schemas: `channels: List[dict{label,samples}]`, EDF field is `b64` (not data_b64). Web status returns `{uplink:'online', detail:'HTTP 200'}`. Chat plot autosynth renders even on LOCAL-CORE budget-exhausted reply because hook appends before storage. Frontend boot takes ~10s.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Initial 5 pytest failures were test-side schema assumptions (fixed by aligning to actual Pydantic models). One transient UI race on rapid substrate button clicks was not reproducible standalone.
